prompt_inputs.content: This paper presents a novel approach to mitigating adversarial perturbations in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) through adversarial training with FGSM and PGD attacks. We employ ResNet-50 architecture with batch normalization layers and implement certified defenses using randomized smoothing techniques. Our methodology incorporates differential privacy (DP) mechanisms with ε-δ bounds to quantify robustness guarantees. We evaluate performance metrics including clean accuracy, robust accuracy under L∞ perturbations, and certified radius bounds. Comparative analysis with existing defense mechanisms such as TRADES and MART demonstrates superior performance on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets. Additionally, we explore the trade-off between model interpretability and adversarial robustness using attention mechanisms and gradient-based attribution methods (Grad-CAM). Our findings suggest that incorporating knowledge distillation from robust teacher models significantly improves generalization capabilities while maintaining computational efficiency on edge devices.
